items.label: Jazz Pharmaceuticals Wells Fargo conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Head of IR John Bluth on business development: the focus is

set.signal: Head of IR John Bluth on business development: the focus is rare disease where Jazz has competency in epilepsy, sleep and oncology, citing over the past 12 to 18 months the Chimerix acquisition (Modeyso), the Saniona acquisition of early epilepsy opportunities, the AbCellera deal in oncology and, most recently, Actio Biosciences in epilepsy. Outside its core areas Jazz is 'less likely to go very early' and more likely to look at proof of concept or later; inside them it is open to earlier transactions and closer-to-commercial deals - 'Look for more from us going forward.' CCO Sam Pearce expects 'very significant commercial synergies' from Actio's KCNT1 epilepsy asset, which shares the core call point with pediatric epileptologists that Epidiolex has; she said additional commercial investments have not yet been detailed. Bluth added that as the Actio transaction closes, the Jazz team will step in and drive the program forward.

items.reason: Attribution: the 'Jazz team will drive the program forward' remark was made by Head of IR John Bluth, not the CCO.
items.evidence: John Bluth, Head of Investor Relations: As we get through the closing of the transaction with Actio, the Jazz team will step in and drive the program forward

items.label: Jazz Pharmaceuticals citigroup summit 2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CCO Samantha Pearce on Epidiolex: the remaining in-label opp

set.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on Epidiolex: the remaining in-label opportunity is particularly the adult long-term care segment, where many LGS patients do not yet have a definitive diagnosis, so Jazz has invested in tools that help physicians diagnose LGS; enrollment in JazzCares extends persistency. She expects the capsule formulation to bring both some conversion of oral-solution patients and incremental growth in the adult segment, without being specific, and said access 'has always been very strong for Epidiolex.' Of the four Epidiolex studies she sized two new populations: 'about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients' in the phase III DEE segment and JME 'around about 60,000 U.S. patients'; the JME study uses the capsule formulation.

items.reason: The CCO sized only two of the four studies' populations (DEE and JME), not all four.
items.evidence: If you look at the phase III DEE study, for example, there are about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients in that particular segment. JME would be between around about 60,000 U.S. patients.

items.label: Jazz Pharmaceuticals citigroup summit 2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CCO Samantha Pearce on the Actio ABS-1230 KCNT1 epilepsy ass

set.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on the Actio ABS-1230 KCNT1 epilepsy asset (she said the deal still needs to close): around 2,500 U.S. patients are diagnosed with KCNT1 epilepsy and, she thinks, prevalence is similar outside the U.S., making it 'an exciting global opportunity for Jazz'; testing is already reflexive for children with epilepsy, and patients can have potentially 100 or so seizures a day. Jazz executive John said Jazz is 'seeing a lot of substrate, especially in epilepsy and oncology', has the balance-sheet capacity for more deals, sets no limits on geography in sourcing, and would fully maximize any asset with broader-than-rare potential, as with Ziihera.
set.figure: around 2,500 U.S. KCNT1 epilepsy patients; prevalence outside the U.S. similar (CCO: 'I think')

items.reason: Hedge restored ('I think') on ex-U.S. prevalence, and 'still to close' attributed to the CCO (the other executive, John, said in the same talk 'we've just completed the Actio deal').
items.evidence: But in the U.S., there are around 2,500 patients that are diagnosed with KCNT1 epilepsy. The prevalence, I think, is similar outside of the U.S. as well.

items.label: MP Materials canaccord growth conference 2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO on heavy rare earths: engineering of the heavy separatio

set.signal: CFO on heavy rare earths: engineering of the heavy separation capability started in 2021; cells are being filled and commissioning is in full swing, with the intention of having on-spec dysprosium and terbium product to bring to Independence within this year. Since NdPr refining began MP has been producing and stockpiling SEG+ (samarium, europium, gadolinium and everything heavier); separating Dy and Tb out creates an SEG fraction and a yttrium holmium plus fraction. Samarium separation from the SEG (committed in the Department of Defense partnership) will be ready for production at the beginning of 2028; MP has since added a long-term contract with a leading aerospace and defense firm to produce separated gadolinium on a long-term basis; CFO: the yttrium holmium plus products also have real use cases and are 'starting to be viewed as very strategic commodities' — 'hopefully there'll be more to come there'.

items.reason: Tense: the source describes a contract to produce separated gadolinium (separation not yet in production), not gadolinium currently being supplied.
items.evidence: The exciting thing that we've since added on is a long-term contract with a leading aerospace and defense firm to produce separated gadolinium on a long-term basis.
